metadata.title: भारत-बर्मा सीमा और ट्राइबल पहचान | Fencing of India Myanmar Border and Tribal ties across border
metadata.description:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced on February 8th that the Government has decided to abolish the Free Movement Regime (FMR) along the Myanmar border. Under the Free Movement Regime, individuals belonging to hill tribes, who are citizens of either India or Myanmar and reside within 16 kilometers of the border on either side, are permitted to cross with the production of a border pass. Typically valid for a year, this pass allows a stay of up to two weeks per visit. This decision by the central government will undoubtedly have significant implications for the tribal communities residing along this border. The cessation of the Free Movement Regime will likely disrupt their traditional ways of life and alter their longstanding patterns of cross-border interaction. It may also challenge their economic activities, which often rely on cross-border trade and movement.
Moreover, the suspension of FMR could potentially strain the socio-cultural ties that these communities have cultivated across the border over generations. The abrupt halt to this regime may lead to feelings of isolation and marginalization among the affected tribal populations.
